name: Bench: Command: Animates (805871) credits the necromancer for a minion kill without a swing
contract: SoloKill.RequirePlayerHit (#10365, default 1) gives an ungrouped player experience from a creature only if they 'hit' it themselves (Creature::AddDirectPlayerAttacker, Spell.cpp:3130 / Unit.cpp:1317). Command: Animates 805871 is NOT caught by AscensionNecromancer::Command()'s SpellFamilyName/flag check (its family flags do not carry the Command bit), but AscensionNecromancerAbilities.cpp's Hit() special-cases id==500991 || id==805871 and routes it through Order() exactly like a real Command (AscensionNecromancerSummons.cpp Responds() answers it for any non-Stationary minion). A level-60 necromancer raises one Greater Skeletal Warrior (51065, via Raise: Greater Skeletal Warrior 504901) and never swings; Command: Animates on a weak creature lets the warrior kill it alone. This bench proves on unfixed main whether that commanded kill gives the necromancer experience (intended behaviour, 'option A': every Command order counts as the player's hit). 805871's only effect targets TARGET_UNIT_TARGET_ALLY (Spell.dbc EffectImplicitTargetA[0]=21), so casting it at a hostile explicit target is refused with SPELL_FAILED_BAD_TARGETS (reason 12); this scenario instead selects the hostile creature (so Order()'s target fallback resolves to it) and casts 805871 at the minion itself via target_owned_entry, matching the spell's real ally-target shape.

steps.label: SETUP: the Greater Skeletal Warrior exists
Command: Animates (805871) cast at the (ally) minion, with the hostile creature selected
BENCH: the commanded kill gives experience
BENCH: the necromancer's level is unchanged
